     3|description: Generate app icons, capture App Store screenshots, and add Xcode targets. Read this before generating icons, screenshots, or adding Swift targets.

     6|## App Configuration
     7|
     8|You just unlocked the `generateIcon`, `captureAppScreenshots`, and `swiftAddTarget` tools.
     9|
    10|### `generateIcon`
    11|
    12|Generates and saves an app icon into the correct project asset structure. Always runs in background — returns a generationId immediately. Call `waitImageResult` with the generationId to collect the result.
    13|
    14|- `appPath`: which app folder (e.g. `"expo"`, `"ios"`)
    15|- `prompt`: describe the icon design
    16|- `iconType`: `"icon"` (main app icon), `"tvos-icon"`, `"visionos-icon"`, or `"imessage-icon"`
    17|
    18|For Swift apps: saves into `Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/icon.png` for all Xcode targets.
    19|For React Native apps: saves into `assets/images/icon.png` and adaptive icon variants.
    20|
    21|tvOS/visionOS/iMessage icon types read the existing app icon from disk and transform it -- generate the main icon first with `iconType: "icon"`, then call again with `"tvos-icon"`, `"visionos-icon"`, or `"imessage-icon"` to populate platform-specific assets.
    22|
    23|### `captureAppScreenshots`
    24|
    25|Captures real app screenshots via an iOS simulator and generates marketing-quality App Store screenshots.
    26|
    27|Before calling this tool read `skills/app-config/screenshots.md` for the full screenshot workflow: exploration strategy, marketing prompt guidelines, and upload instructions.
    28|
    29|### `swiftAddTarget`
    30|
    31|Adds a new target to an Xcode project. Supports widgets (WidgetKit), share extensions, notification content extensions, app intent extensions, watchOS apps, tvOS apps, visionOS apps, and iMessage apps.
    32|
    33|- `name`: target name in PascalCase (e.g. `"MyAppWidget"`, `"MyAppShare"`)
    34|- `type`: the target type to add
    35|- `path`: app folder containing the Xcode project (defaults to the main app)
    36|
    37|The tool creates the target, sets up build settings, adds a dependency from the host app, embeds the extension, and creates minimal scaffold source files. After calling this tool, write the actual Swift code for the target and call `swiftBuild` to verify the project compiles.
    38|
